about: Every word the Nashville row, the chip line, the HUD's plain half and the practice verbs may print (theory-nextgen-spec D10, 2.6; TN0, frozen after TN0, changes go through the conductor). Plain word first, theory name second (dropped first on overflow). Spec 3.2 wins over design-pedagogy 6.2 where they differ: the row says 'new key' (not 'new home') and 'outside <key>' for chromatic chords (not 'far outside'). The canvas draws row words in capitals; stored words are lower case. Scale and key names are addresses, not face words.

guard.rule: case-insensitive whole words (and % anywhere) never appear in plain, theory, meaning or caption examples; the symbols never appear either (D12, design-pedagogy 6.1 rule 6). Sources: jam-spec 11.4 and spec 2.6 for the first eight words, design-pedagogy 6.1 rule 3 for the last three.

caption_grammar: <number>   <run> · <run> · <run>. Each run is a lexicon entry's plain or theory part, or a slot. Overflow drops the runs whose role is theory first, then key; plain runs stay. One caption at a time, by priority (D8).
